title: Manvir Singh Hat Trick Powers Mohun Bagan to 8-0 Rout of South United in Durand Cup
excerpt: The ISL champions sealed their place in the knockout round with a commanding Group A victory at Kolkata's Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan.
body:
• Mohun Bagan Super Giant demolished South United 8-0 in their Durand Cup Group A match on August 4, with Manvir Singh scoring a hat trick (4', 22', 60').
  • Rahul Bheke (19', 36'), Alberto Rodriguez (10'), Suhail Ahmad Bhat (89', 90+1'), and an own goal from South United's Noel (70') completed the rout.
  • Mohun Bagan have now won both their group matches with nine goals scored and none conceded, securing qualification to the knockout stage.
  • The 135th edition of Asia's oldest football tournament continues through August 23.

Mohun Bagan Super Giant sent an emphatic statement to the rest of the Durand Cup field on Tuesday evening, dismantling South United 8-0 in a Group A encounter that was effectively over before halftime.

Manvir Sets the Tone

India international Manvir Singh needed just four minutes to open the scoring at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan in Kolkata, and he never let up. His clinical hat trick — goals in the 4th, 22nd, and 60th minutes — earned him the Man of the Match award and underlined why the ISL champions' attack is the most feared in Indian football right now.

Alberto Rodriguez doubled the lead in the 10th minute before captain Rahul Bheke joined the party with a brace of his own in the 19th and 36th minutes. By halftime, Mohun Bagan led 4-0 and the contest was done.

Second Half Avalanche

The Mariners showed no mercy after the break. Manvir completed his treble on the hour mark, and an own goal from South United's Noel in the 70th minute made it six. Substitute Suhail Ahmad Bhat added a late double in the 89th and 91st minutes to put a historic gloss on the scoreline.

South United, a Bangalore-based club making their Durand Cup debut, were simply outclassed in every department. The I-League Division 2 side had earned a creditable 2-0 win over CISF Protectors in their opening match but found the gap between themselves and an ISL powerhouse impossible to bridge.

Group A Picture

The result leaves Mohun Bagan top of Group A with a perfect six points from two matches, nine goals scored and zero conceded. East Bengal, who beat Mohun Bagan's city rivals 8-0 in their own demolition of CISF Protectors, sit second with three points. The two Kolkata giants had already met in the group's marquee fixture on July 25, with Mohun Bagan edging a tight 1-0 derby win before 32,870 fans.

Mohun Bagan's final group match against CISF Protectors on August 10 is now a formality, with the Mariners already through to the knockout rounds.

Durand Cup Context

The 135th edition of Asia's oldest football tournament, now branded the IndianOil Durand Cup 2026, runs through August 23. Defending champions, Mohun Bagan are looking to add another trophy to a cabinet that already includes last season's ISL title. Tuesday's performance — disciplined in defence, devastating in attack — suggests they remain the team to beat.
